<description>
`CTxMemPool::GetSortedScoreWithTopology()` gets the global mempool order with a `std::sort` that uses `TxGraph::CompareMainOrder` as comparator. This is N log N comparisons, and it runs with `cs` held. It is used by `getrawmempool`, the P2P `mempool` message, `mempool.dat` dumping and `check()`.

`TxGraph` already keeps all main chunks in an index ordered by `ChunkOrder` (`m_main_chunkindex`), which is the same order as `CompareMainOrder`. This PR adds `TxGraph::GetMainOrder()`, which walks that index and expands each chunk in linearization order. The result is all transactions in `CompareMainOrder` order, in O(N) and with no comparator calls. `GetSortedScoreWithTopology()` now uses it. The old sort is kept in `check()` as an assert that both orders are equal.

The order is the same, so there is no change in RPC, P2P or `mempool.dat` output.

I ran some preliminar experiments and got:

Ryzen 5 3600, x86:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `RpcMempoolTxids` (10k txs) | 5.10 ms | 1.07 ms |
| `getrawmempool false` handler, 60k txs | 99 ms | 24 ms |

Most of the remaining time in `RpcMempoolTxids` is building the JSON array, not the order. `getrawmempool true` does not change much because `entryToJSON` dominates. The time with `cs` held goes down in the same way, which matters for indexers that call `getrawmempool` every few seconds.
</description>

<commits>
98b1610173 bench: add RpcMempoolTxids

Benchmark getrawmempool without verbose on a mempool made of chains of
25 transactions. This covers the cost of ordering the entries, which
RpcMempool does not show.

7a3420d4ef txgraph: add GetMainOrder

Return all transactions in the main graph in the order of
CompareMainOrder by walking the chunk index, without comparing
transactions. The unit test and the fuzz test check that it matches the
order of a BlockBuilder that skips nothing, and the fuzz test also
checks the order implied by CompareMainOrder.

a007033a9f txmempool: get main order from TxGraph::GetMainOrder

GetSortedScoreWithTopology() sorted all entries with
TxGraph::CompareMainOrder, which does pairwise comparisons across
clusters. Ask the TxGraph for the main order instead, which it already
has in its chunk index. check() keeps the comparison sort as a
reference and asserts that both orders agree.
</commits>
